subsystems.name: Sensor array
subsystems.role: picks up the tiny electrical signals that muscles in the finger generate when they contract.

subsystems.name: Signal processing and AI
subsystems.role: filters noise and turns raw muscle signals into intended commands.

subsystems.name: Power
subsystems.role: keeps the ring running for a day or more on a tiny battery.
parts: charging contacts or wireless charging coil

subsystems.name: Communication
subsystems.role: sends commands wirelessly to a phone, computer or headset.

subsystems.name: Mechanical housing
subsystems.role: fits comfortably on a finger and holds electrodes against the skin.
parts: biocompatible ring body (metal or engineering plastic)

buildSteps.title: Map the muscle signals
buildSteps.detail: Study which finger and hand muscles produce distinct electrical patterns for different gestures, and where on the finger they can be sensed.

buildSteps.title: Design the electrode layout
buildSteps.detail: Place several small dry electrodes around the inside of the ring so they touch the skin without gel and resist movement.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the ring body
buildSteps.detail: Mould or machine a biocompatible shell that holds the electrodes, electronics and battery in a package a few millimetres thick.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the electronics
buildSteps.detail: Solder the analog front-end, microcontroller, radio and power management onto a tiny rigid-flex circuit board that curves around the finger.

buildSteps.title: Collect training data
buildSteps.detail: Record muscle signals from many people performing a set of intended gestures, then train a machine-learning model to classify them.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate per user
buildSteps.detail: Because every person's muscle signals differ, run a short calibration session that adapts the model to the wearer.

buildSteps.title: Test accuracy and comfort
buildSteps.detail: Measure how often the ring correctly recognises a gesture, how long it takes, and whether it stays comfortable during hours of wear.

buildSteps.title: Iterate and shrink
buildSteps.detail: Reduce power consumption, improve electrode contact, and miniaturise the electronics until the ring is unobtrusive and reliable.

prerequisites.why: they pick up muscle signals without conductive gel, which is essential for a wearable ring.
they run gesture-recognition models on a battery small enough to fit in a ring.
models work in controlled tests but still struggle with sweat, motion and differences between users.
it provides a low-energy wireless link to phones and headsets.
they supply enough energy for a day of intermittent use in a very small volume.

pathway.milestone: research prototypes recognise a handful of gestures in the lab
pathway.unlocks: proof that a ring can read finger muscle signals reliably enough to control a simple interface.

pathway.milestone: user-independent models and longer battery life
pathway.unlocks: practical hands-free control for augmented reality, virtual reality and accessibility tools.

pathway.milestone: integration with mainstream phones, headsets and computers
pathway.unlocks: everyday use without special calibration or setup.

pathway.milestone: seamless, always-on neural interfaces that combine muscle signals with other biosignals
pathway.unlocks: intuitive, invisible control of digital devices as a natural extension of the hand.
